ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto-Ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, adapting the Spanish legal framework to EU directives; Ley 19/2021, de 20 de diciembre, establishing the Registro de Titularidades Reales; Directive (EU) 2018/843 (Fifth AML Directive) transposition measures; Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Mercantile Registry Regulations) and Circular 3/2022 of the Bank of Spain concerning corporate due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or similar authority in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for incorporation and representation before Spanish Notary and Mercantile Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all individual UBOs and subscribing shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary or competent consular official in the document holder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if non-Hague party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed UBO declaration and corporate ownership chain disclosure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representatives of each shareholder up to the ultimate natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in country of origin plus Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Tax Residence of foreign shareholders, where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation of all foreign-language corporate documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator appointed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation or registered with the Ministry of Justice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required for the translation itself; original document authentication must precede translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of shareholders, directors, authorized representatives, and UBOs against the Spanish Seguridad y Vigilancia de Entidades Financieras system, Bank of Spain risk lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council sanctions, and the OFAC SDN List when international banks or US payment rails (Stripe, credit card acquiring) are involved. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs under FATF Recommendation 12 and Directive (EU) 2015/849 as transposed. The screening must be documented and retained for at least 10 years after business relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central online certification system (Denominaciones Sociales)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Real Decreto 1784/1996, article 178, corporate names must not infringe public order or mislead as to the entity's identity. The name must be stated in Spanish, or in any language generally usable in international commerce provided a Spanish transliteration is submitted where the script is non-Latin. The chosen name must produce a certificate of non-coincidence issued by the Registro Mercantil Central before the notarial deeds are executed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central issues a negative certification, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month from notification of the refusal, under Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del Procedimiento Administrativo Común. The appeal must be filed electronically through the portal of the Ministry of Justice, attaching the refused application, certificate, and a memorandum of law. As an alternative, the applicant may immediately file a new application with a different proposed name; no formal extension of a positive reservation is available beyond the statutory validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole Spanish registered office for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The mercantile registry requires a physical address within a Spanish municipality where the actual management or control is exercisable or, in accordance with Article 9 of Royal Decree 1784/1996, where a typical professional office can be inspected. A virtual address may be used only as an auxiliary mail-forwarding facility and must not be listed as the registered domicile in the incorporation deed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 8-12% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by Agencia Tributaria or the Spanish Tax Agency within the first 12 months of registration, and approximately 5% probability of a Social Security/Treasury inspection during the same period for low-risk commercial entities; these inspections are triggered by inconsistencies in commercial substance or registered-office disclosures.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance application fee (certificación de denominación social) to Registro Mercantil Central
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Spain's applicable fee schedule for mercantile registry services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign corporate document apostille and legalization fees, assuming six documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document official fee varying by jurisdiction; estimated at USD 30 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator registered with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 80-120 per page depending on complexity and number of documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE application fee for foreign incorporators or legal representatives
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreigners' Office of the Spanish National Police or the relevant consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee, currently EUR 10-11 converted to USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fees for the incorporation deed (escritura de constitución)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) in the selected registration district
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff scale based on share capital and deed complexity; estimated between EUR 500 and EUR 700

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional registration and filing fees before the Provincial Mercantile Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory mercantile registry tariff calculated on a sliding scale; estimated for a standard limited-liability company with share capital of EUR 3,000-30,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing (declaración de titularidad real)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / Registro de Titularidades Reales
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative processing fee and compliance filing, subject to periodic governmental fee updates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIF/CIF provisional tax-identification application for the company (Modelo 036 filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for the filing itself; estimated cost represents professional processing and legal assistance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation corporate due diligence, drafting of articles of association, and legal opinion by Spanish law counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish law firm authorized to appear before the Mercantile Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark quoted as a fixed professional fee for a standard low-risk SL incorporation with one foreign corporate shareholder

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening compliance and OFAC/PEP screening facilitation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank or payment institution, not a public registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for supporting documentation and compliance review; official bank charges vary from EUR 50 to EUR 150

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC) — Arts. 12-14 (minimum capital and paid-in rules), 20-22 (deed and registration), 28-39 (bylaws), 62 (subscription and payment), 137 (administration); Ley 18/2022, de 28 de septiembre, de creación y crecimiento de empresas (Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva regime); Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores (fast-track SL); Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the registered office's judicial province, e.g., Registro Mercantil de Madrid; Registro Mercantil Central for the negative name certificate and BORME publication; Ministry of Justice (Ministerio de Justicia) as supervisory authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public incorporation deed) together with the Estatutos sociales (corporate bylaws), executed before a Spanish Notary and presented for inscription at the Registro Mercantil Provincial; preceded by certificación negativa de denominación social and followed by NIF assignment (Modelo 036) and mandatory publication in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SL: minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid-in in cash at incorporation, evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit (certificado de depósito) per LSC Art. 62. Under the Ley 18/2022 SLFS regime, incorporation with capital below EUR 3,000 is permitted but distributions are restricted until such amount is reached and the company must allocate 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve. Capital contributions may not consist of services; increases or decreases require public deed and registry inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 1/2025 — RESOLVED: (1) The shareholders accept the subscription of 3,000 registered participation units of €1.00 par value, and certify that the entire share capital is paid in by bank deposit pursuant to Articles 62 and 78 of the Capital Companies Law. (2) The registered office is adopted at Avenida de la Innovación 15, 28050 Madrid. (3) Mr. Alejandro Serra is appointed Managing Director, Ms. Elena Vidal is appointed Corporate Secretary, and Mr. Nikola Petrov is appointed Non-executive Director, all accepting their offices. (4) The Managing Director is delegated authority to open payment-rail accounts, hire compliance advisers, apply for the definitive tax code, and obtain municipal operating permits. (5) All pre-incorporation costs are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Vetting and Negative Name Certification (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central — Departamento de Denominaciones Sociales (online via Registradores de España or through any authorized Notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the denomination certificate application electronically stating the corporate form SL, proposed corporate names (up to three alternatives), corporate object describing the assembly of interactive bionic pet robots (CNAE 3240), registered-office province, and full identities of promoters. Pay the application fee. The certificate is valid for six months and must be attached to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Application form for corporate name certificate (solicitud de certificación de denominación social)
Description of corporate purpose under CNAE/ISIC 3240
Passport or NIE copies of founding shareholders
Alternative name proposals in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for identity or undue similarity, the Registrar issues a note and the applicant may present additional alternative names or appeal within twenty business days; a corrected application under the same priority number resolves the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Constitution Bank Account and Share Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution of the promoters' choice branch located in the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute provisional account opening in the name '[Company Name], S.L. En Constitución' presenting the negative name certificate and draft bylaws. All shareholders or their legal representatives sign the account mandate. Pay in at least EUR 3,000 as paid-up share capital. Obtain the bank's deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) identifying each contributing shareholder and the deposited sums for attachment to the deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Draft estatutos sociales
Identification documents of all shareholders or representatives
Proof of domicile and tax residence of each shareholder
Initial capital contribution of EUR 3,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines for KYC/AML reasons, supply beneficial-ownership declarations or apostilled notarial identity certificates, or open the account with another credit institution; non-resident shareholders must first obtain an NIE number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution before Notary Public of the Public Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public authorized to practice in Spain (Colegio Notarial) in the notarial district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding partners attend personally or by notarized representative to sign the escritura de constitución and estatutos. The notary verifies legal capacity, capital payment, and compliance with LSC mandatory provisions. The deed identifies every partner, specifies the corporate object (ISIC 3240), registered office, subscribed and paid-in capital, administrative structure, accounting year, and governance clauses. First and second authorized copies are issued for registration and tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of negative denomination valid six months
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Draft articles of association including ISIC 3240 corporate object
Passport/NIE of all shareholders and appointed directors
Notarial powers of attorney where representatives act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects, execute a supplementary corrective deed (subsanación) or re-sign the instrument; absent shareholders may act through notarial representation letters; capital shortfalls are cured by re-depositing funds and producing a revised bank certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados (Modalidad Operaciones Societarias)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax authority of the Autonomous Community where the registered office is located (e.g., Agencia Tributaria de la Comunidad de Madrid; Departament d'Economia i Hisenda de la Generalitat de Catalunya)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Modelo 600 self-assessment electronically within thirty business days of the deed date declaring the paid-in capital and the provisional NIF. Pay 1% of nominal share capital as the corporate-operations transfer tax. Obtain the proof-of-payment receipt for submission to the Commercial Registry where required.
required_dossiers: First authorized copy of the public deed
Second copy for the tax authority
Modelo 600 self-assessment form
Provisional NIF certificate
Bank certificate evidencing payment means
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority finds rate or taxable-base errors, submit a rectification form and pay the differential amount; overpayments are recovered through the solicitud de rectificación y devolución de ingresos indebidos within four years.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Deed in the Provincial Commercial Registry (Inscripción en el Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office; publication in BORME by the Registro Mercantil Central
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month from notarial grant, present the first authorized copy and the duplicate copy to the provincial registry along with the Modelo 600 receipt and provisional NIF. The registrar performs legal qualification; upon inscription the SL acquires full legal personality. The registration is published in BORME, and a nota simple registral is obtained as formal legal evidence.
required_dossiers: First authorized copy of the established deed
Duplicate copy of the deed for the Registry
Justification of ITP-AJD tax payment
Provisional NIF certificate
Negative name certificate appended to the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a suspensive or negative qualification, submit a corrective notarial deed curing the defects within the suspension deadline; late presentation beyond one month is admitted by the Administration but may give rise to sanction proceedings, without loss of legal effects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive Tax Identification Number (NIF Definitivo) and Census Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Delegación/Agencia at the corporate fiscal address; electronic filing via Sede Electrónica or assisted appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, file Modelo 036/037 declaración censal to update the corporate status, IAE activity code for CNAE 3240, address, and legal representatives. AEAT assigns the definitive NIF linked to the registered legal name. Withdraw the definitive NIF certificate in person or through a duly appointed representative; the NIF is mandatory for invoicing, contracts, and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate or nota simple of Commercial Registry registration
Modelo 036 declaración censal
Identification and power of attorney of the legal representative
Registered address proof
Appointment confirmation at the AEAT office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT raises census anomalies, submit a complementary Modelo 036 rectifying the data; if the NIF withdrawal appointment is delayed, use the representative procedure with notarial power or obtain the certificate electronically via the corporate electronic seal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Activity License — Prior Communication and Operating License (Licencia de Actividad y Apertura)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality where the assembly plant is located (e.g., Madrid: Agencia de Actividades; Barcelona: Departament de Llicències d'Activitats)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the declaración responsable / comunicación previa or, for classified installations, the licencia de actividad accompanied by a technical memorandum covering premises dimensions, machinery layout, noise insulation, fire compartments, electrical load, accessibility, and waste collection. Municipal technicians verify the file and issue the licencia de apertura; low-risk assembly operations may commence upon confirmed receipt of the declaration.
required_dossiers: Municipal application form or responsible declaration
Technical report describing the ISIC 3240 robotic toy assembly process
Fire safety certificate per CTE DB-SI
Low-voltage electrical installation certificate per RD 842/2002
Building occupancy/urbanistic compatibility certificate
Waste producer registration and environmental communication where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality raises objections on noise, vibration, urbanistic incompatibility, or neighbor interference, submit an amended technical file and, where required, appeal before the municipal plenary (recurso de alzada); the deadline is suspended during the corrective procedure and the license is issued once non-conformities are cured.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria y de la PYME of the Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo (national technical safety and market surveillance for toys); the autonomous community's Consejería de Industria (industrial installation communications under Ley 21/1992, de Industria); and the municipal licensing department (Ayuntamiento) for the activity opening license at the physical plant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de apertura y funcionamiento (municipal operating license) / Comunicación previa de inicio de actividad industrial under Ley 21/1992, complemented by CE product conformity under the Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/CE transposed by Real Decreto 1151/2011, de 29 de julio, on toy safety.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the autonomous community where the plant is located (e.g., Comunidad de Madrid — Dirección General de Sostenibilidad y Economía Circular; Generalitat de Catalunya — Direcció General de Qualitat Ambiental), with technical supervision by the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) and municipal environmental services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA Report required under Ley 21/2013 Annexes I or II for this scale of toy assembly, unless solvent-coating lines exceed 15 t/year of organic solvent use (Annex II category 4.2), in which case a simplified environmental impact assessment applies. Standard file: Comunicación ambiental previa to the local council and mandatory registration as waste producer under Ley 7/2022, de residuos.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: (i) Wastewater: any process discharge to municipal sewer must meet municipal by-laws and typical thresholds — pH 6-9, temperature < 40 °C, total suspended solids ≤ 300 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 400 mg/L, COD ≤ 750 mg/L; no hazardous liquid discharge. (ii) VOC: if solvent-based paints or adhesives are used, comply with RD 117/2003 emission limit values and fugitive-emission caps (≤ 20-25% of solvent input) with records when consumption exceeds 2 t/year; threshold of 15 t/year triggers EIA. (iii) Waste: packaging waste under RD 1055/2022, WEEE registration under RD 110/2015 for electronic components, battery management under RD 710/2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety technical certificate per Código Técnico de la Edificación (RD 314/2006 DB-SI/DB-SUA) presented to the municipal civil defense department; structural load certificate validating floor capacities for the robotic assembly lines; workplace risk-prevention plan under Ley 31/1995 with emergency procedures and health-and-safety audit; low-voltage electrical installation certificate (RD 842/2002 REBT); machinery conformity certificate (RD 1644/2008 transposing Directive 2006/42/EC).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Spanish State Tax Administration Agency; electronic headquarters: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), obtain a provisional NIF through the notary/company registry prior to incorporation; after public deed and registration with the Mercantile Registry, file AEAT Modelo 036 to apply for definitive NIF and inscription in the official Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Withholders. A Spanish resident legal representative and a Spanish tax notification address are required. The NIF doubles as Spanish VAT ID when the company carries out taxable business activities; an EORI number must also be requested if goods exports are planned. For non-resident entities without a permanent establishment, direct VAT/NIF registration is made using Modelo 036 with the same electronic channel or through the applicable simplified registration forms; registration is required before any taxable supply in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: a Spanish-resident SL is a separate taxpayer fully liable to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income, with foreign tax relief; non-resident shareholders are subject only to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on Spanish-source items. The SL is not pass-through eligible.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box election. Available elections include: tax consolidation regime for groups meeting the 80% voting/equity threshold; accelerated depreciation; patent box regime for qualifying IP; merger/asset-contribution neutrality election; ETVE holding regime; SOCIMI listing election; and foreign tax credit rather than deduction election in some cases. Hybrid mismatch treatment under ATAD implementation is mandatory and cannot be eliminated by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) – Spanish value added tax under Ley 37/1992, harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC (mainland Spain; Canary Islands/Ceuta/Melilla have separate IGIC/IPSI regimes)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold exists for Spanish-established suppliers: VAT registration via Modelo 036 is compulsory before commencing any business activity. For non-established EU sellers engaged in intra-EU distance sales or electronic services, the OSS registration threshold is EUR 10,000 if the seller is established in another Member State; for non-EU sellers any supply creates registration nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not operate a transaction-by-transaction tax-stamping or pre-clearance model. The AEAT operates the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) requiring large taxpayers and VAT groups to submit invoice-level data electronically within 4 calendar days after issue; the B2C/B2B e-invoicing mandate is implemented through Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) using structured electronic invoice formats such as FacturaE XML. The VeriFactu framework requires billing software to generate tamper-evident, hash-linked invoice records accessible to AEAT. For public-sector invoices, the FACe platform and its API/interoperability requirements are mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for the export exemption with right to deduct input VAT (economically 0% IVA) where the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the European Union by the supplier, the customer, or a third party on their behalf, evidenced by the customs export declaration and transport documentation. Offshore and export-related services may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT or exempt where the recipient is established outside the EU under the B2B place-of-supply rules; the supplier must hold documentary evidence of the customer’s non-EU status, the nature of the service, and, where required, effective use and exploitation outside Spain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (DUA / Single Administrative Document) validated by Spanish Customs and evidencing definitive export from the EU
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) or CMR road consignment note showing carriage out of the EU
Commercial invoice and export packing list
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident purchaser
Exporter’s NIF/VAT ID and EORI registration evidence
Certificate of origin / EUR.1 or Form A where a preferential origin claim is made
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT rigorously audits export zero-rating files and may claw back deducted input VAT plus assess undeclared output VAT at 21% if export evidence is deficient, false, or not timely retained. Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the VAT prejudice depending on concealment; late-payment interest accrues from the original due date; the four-year tax verification statute gives AEAT retrospective clawback power. Criminal liability under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code can apply (prison terms of 2–6 years) where defrauded VAT exceeds EUR 120,000. Exporters should retain the complete DUA/customs/B/L/payment record file for at least the statutory limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-investment and external-payment reporting is also administered under the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise, including the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted within the euro area and generally unrestricted for cross-border commercial payments to third countries, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, payment-screening requirements, and bank documentation. Capital movements are liberalized under EU law and Spanish foreign-exchange legislation. An Spanish SL may generally receive foreign capital, hold foreign-currency accounts, pay foreign suppliers, distribute dividends, repay shareholder loans, and remit liquidation proceeds, provided corporate approvals, distributable-profit rules, withholding-tax requirements, beneficial-owner verification, transfer-pricing requirements, and applicable foreign-investment or external-transaction reporting are satisfied. Banks may require evidence of the capital contribution, loan agreement, dividend resolution, tax clearance or withholding evidence, source of funds, commercial rationale, and ultimate beneficial ownership before executing remittances. Foreign direct investment reporting may apply depending on investor status, ownership percentage, sector, transaction value, origin, and applicable statutory exemptions. Payments involving sanctioned persons, restricted jurisdictions, or unexplained third-party funds may be blocked or reported.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose a general statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds to a Spanish bank or convert a prescribed percentage of export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in euros or foreign currency and may be received into Spanish or appropriately documented foreign accounts. There is no general mandatory conversion ratio or universal statutory repatriation deadline for ordinary goods exports. The company must retain commercial, customs, transport, invoice, and payment records and satisfy applicable VAT, Intrastat, statistical, banking, and anti-money-laundering information requests. Cash or equivalent instruments transported across EU external borders at EUR 10,000 or more must be declared under applicable EU and Spanish cash-control rules. Banks may impose contractual receipt, reconciliation, sanctions-screening, and documentary requirements, and sector-specific or state-support conditions may create additional reporting obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. An EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide EUR accounts, payment services, cards, and international transfers under passporting or local authorization, but it is not a Spanish deposit-taking bank unless separately licensed as a credit institution. Customer funds are generally safeguarded rather than covered by the Spanish deposit-guarantee scheme. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorization or a valid EU passport cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services to the Spanish SL merely through an application interface. Fintech onboarding may be unsuitable for statutory share-capital certification, notarial incorporation evidence, complex shareholder loans, high-value trade finance, cash handling, documentary letters of credit, or transactions involving elevated sanctions, marketplace, or virtual-asset exposure. The company should maintain a regulated Spanish or EU bank as its primary treasury account and use an EMI only as a controlled secondary rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank can perform legally compliant electronic identification, beneficial-owner verification, document authentication, and video or equivalent due diligence. Banks may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, qualified electronic-signature process, notarized or apostilled documents, branch attendance for non-resident directors, or a local authorized signatory. The bank's risk policy controls the practical outcome. A Spanish SL should appoint properly documented representatives, maintain a Spanish registered office and operating rationale, and be prepared for enhanced review where directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, or source funds are foreign.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ownership chain, nominee shareholders, unexplained control rights, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified current extract from the Spanish Commercial Registry; articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart through every intermediate entity to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and proof of address for beneficial owners and directors; beneficial-owner declaration; powers of attorney; and explanation of voting and control arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or director with documents that are expired, untranslated, unauthenticated, or inconsistent across jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports or national identity documents; recent address evidence; apostilled or legalized corporate certificates where required; sworn Spanish translations where requested; incumbency and good-standing certificates; board resolutions; notarized powers of attorney; and a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction identity reconciliation memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of capital, shareholder loans, unusually large initial deposits, or third-party funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or loan agreement; shareholder and board approvals; bank statements showing the funding trail; audited financial statements or tax returns of the funding party; sale-of-asset or investment documentation where relevant; source-of-wealth narrative; sanctions screening; and a transaction-purpose statement tying the funds to incorporation, inventory, payroll, or operating expenditure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model perceived as inconsistent with the stated activity, including robotics, artificial intelligence, consumer electronics, online sales, marketplaces, or high-volume card payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; product specifications; supplier and customer contracts; website and domain ownership evidence; warehouse or logistics agreements; distribution model; expected monthly transaction volumes; average ticket size; countries of operation; refund and chargeback policy; applicable product-safety and conformity documentation; and management experience profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, restricted counterparties, unusual intermediaries, or mismatched payer and beneficiary names.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC files; beneficial-owner evidence; contracts, purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading, customs records, and end-user statements; sanctions and adverse-media screening; payment-flow diagram; explanation of any intermediary; and documented compliance approval before execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected export or import activity without a coherent customs, VAT, and transaction-reconciliation process.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EORI registration where required; VAT registration details; sample commercial invoices; Incoterms; customs-broker agreement; transport documents; import and export workflow; inventory records; VAT and Intrastat procedures; bank reconciliation policy; and responsible-person matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple foreign accounts, use of personal accounts, payment-service-provider accounts, or unexplained transfers between affiliated entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; approved account list; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing support; account-purpose matrix; monthly reconciliation procedures; evidence that personal accounts are not used for corporate receipts; and documented approval controls for intercompany payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative media, politically exposed person status, regulatory history, insolvency indicators, or adverse information concerning a director, shareholder, supplier, or customer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal and compliance report; explanation and supporting court or regulatory documents; remediation evidence; enhanced-monitoring plan; updated corporate certificates; PEP declaration; wealth and income evidence; and senior-management approval of the residual-risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Application for a capital account or capital certificate without a finalized incorporation deed, subscription details, or clear account signatory mandate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Draft or executed articles; incorporation deed or notarial appointment; proposed name certificate; founders' identification; capital subscription schedule; bank account-opening mandate; source-of-funds evidence; notary instructions; and post-incorporation plan to convert or link the capital account to the operational account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital through a regulated Spanish or EU bank using SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments where available and SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-SEPA currencies. The payment reference should identify the Spanish SL, the legal basis, and the purpose, such as share-capital subscription, share premium, shareholder loan, or equity contribution. Before receipt, provide the bank with the subscription agreement or loan agreement, corporate resolutions, ownership and beneficial-owner data, source-of-funds evidence, and intended use of proceeds. For incorporation capital, obtain the bank certificate required by the notary or confirm the current notarial evidence route accepted by the relevant bank. After incorporation, record the contribution in the accounting books and statutory corporate records. Reconcile the remitter, payer, and beneficiary names; avoid unrelated third-party remitters; retain MT103 or ISO 20022 payment confirmation; and monitor applicable foreign-investment, external-transaction, tax, and statistical reporting. No general Spanish FX purpose-code regime applies to ordinary euro transfers, but the bank may require an internal payment purpose, supporting invoice, contract, or regulatory declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 for traditional single-payment international transfers where supported; banks are progressively migrating to ISO 20022 payment messages, including pacs.008, so payment instructions should follow the servicing bank's format. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through a regulated bank under UCP 600, with documentary collections under URC 522 where appropriate. Include accurate beneficiary, ultimate payer, invoice, purchase-order, Incoterms, goods description, customs, shipping, and tax information. Use bank guarantees or standby letters of credit only under documented contractual terms and approved facility limits. Reconcile payments against invoices and goods-receipt or shipping evidence, apply segregation of duties and dual authorization, and retain records for tax, customs, AML, accounting, and audit purposes. Avoid cash settlement, personal accounts, unapproved payment agents, and third-party payments without documented commercial justification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forwards with a regulated bank or eligible investment firm, used to hedge identifiable forecast or contracted receivables, payables, capital injections, or intercompany flows.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local convertibility restrictions, where offered by an appropriately regulated counterparty and permitted under the laws governing the currency and transaction.
Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, valuation, collateral, accounting, and applicable EMIR obligations.
Foreign-exchange options, including plain-vanilla calls, puts, and collars, for documented commercial exposures, subject to suitability, disclosure, premium, valuation, and treasury-policy controls.

FX spot transactions and rolling short-dated conversions for operational settlement, provided the company maintains transaction records and does not conduct speculative dealing as an unlicensed financial business.

All derivatives should be governed by an approved treasury policy and, where applicable, an ISDA or equivalent master agreement, confirmation procedures, counterparty limits, collateral terms, mark-to-market controls, hedge-accounting analysis, EMIR reporting or clearing assessment, and board-approved delegation limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de cuentas anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Commercial Registry corresponding to the registered office (Spain)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the shareholders' meeting, and approval is required within six months of the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year companies, the last practical filing date is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If accounts are not filed within 18 months from the fiscal year-end, the registry sheet is closed (cierre registral), preventing registration of any corporate acts (e.g., director reappointments, capital changes, amendments). The company may also face administrative dissolution for continued non-filing. Fiscal penalties and surcharges may apply under tax law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership annual confirmation (Declaración de titularidad real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titularidad Real, managed by the Commercial Registry authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month after the anniversary of the prior registration or upon any change in beneficial ownership, as applicable under Royal Decree 571/2023; the calendar deadline is typically due within 30 days after each annual confirmation trigger.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate beneficial ownership declarations may result in fines up to EUR 60,000 under Spanish money-laundering / beneficial-ownership regulations, and the entity may be prohibited from using certain corporate registry services until compliance is restored.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit is required for companies meeting at least two of the following three criteria for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; net annual turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees exceeds 50. Companies in certain sectors (e.g., banks, insurers, investment funds) are always audited regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish local GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) under the Código de Comercio; consolidated financial statements of listed groups may be prepared in accordance with IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: As of the adoption of Royal Decree 571/2023, every SL must maintain accurate beneficial ownership information in the Registro de Titularidad Real. An annual confirmation must be lodged updating the register whenever the shareholding structure changes or at least annually to confirm the existing beneficial owners. The confirmation must identify each ultimate beneficial owner (name, ID/Passport, nationality, residence, and percentage or nature of control). Failure to lodge the annual confirmation does not automatically restrict share transfers, but share transfers will not be admitted to the commercial register until the UBO register is updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Register of Contracts with the Company (Libro-Registro de Contratos con la Sociedad)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 1,000 – EUR 2,500 (USD 1,100 – USD 2,750) depending on the city and whether registered-office services are bundled with a registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 1,800 – EUR 4,500 (USD 2,000 – USD 5,000) for a small-to-medium SL requiring a statutory audit.

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
